meta.name: Atlas
meta.summary: Atlas turns up to ten photos and a story into a paginated magazine that is composed and printed to PDF entirely in the browser. A React 19 SPA on Vercel talks to one Express 5 API on Render, which checks accounts and allowances against Supabase, calls Anthropic or OpenAI for the AI editor, copy desk and voice, and takes payments through Dodo (or Stripe). Saved issues are sealed in the browser and stored as encrypted page pictures.

flows.name: Sign in with Google
flows.summary: Sign-in is a full-page redirect, so the desk parks itself first and comes back exactly once.

steps.detail: Photos (as File handles), story, theme and every desk choice go into DeskDraft, because the redirect will throw the page away.
prompt=select_account so Google always asks which account; the PKCE verifier is kept in the browser.

steps.text: Redirect back with a Supabase session
steps.detail: Back to the page that asked; the desk reads its parked draft once.
The API client attaches the Supabase access token.
The token is verified by Supabase, never just decoded here.
authenticate stops the request.
active, trialing, past_due and on_hold unlock the plan; newest row wins.
The browser uses the plan only to decide what to show.

flows.name: The AI editor designs an issue
flows.summary: The only call that sends photographs: 512px previews and the story go to the model, a page-by-page plan comes back.

steps.detail: Drawn on a canvas in the browser; the originals never leave.
Up to 10 previews, the story, art direction id and note.
Its own 4 MB JSON parser runs before the 1 MB global one.
Sign-in is on for the editor in src/types.
In-memory sliding window per account.

steps.text: 429 · That was a lot at once
steps.detail: Sends Retry-After.
Photo count, data-URL shape, size caps, theme and face lists, direction id. A bad request is refused before anything is spent.
Then the story is checked against the plan's word limit (413).
One statement decides and increments, so a double-click can't slip two claims past it. Free 2, Traveller 5, Cartographer 12 a month.

steps.text: 402 · That is all of this month's designs

steps.detail: Opus 5.5, adaptive thinking at medium effort, a JSON schema for the plan, and a server-side fallback model if the request is declined. One retry, 150s timeout.
Nothing reached the reader, so the design is given back.
Bounds every number, checks fonts against the list offered, and refuses an answer without a usable design.
Create.tsx applies it with an undo.

flows.name: Export to PDF
flows.summary: Composition is entirely in the browser; the server only counts free accounts' exports before the print sheet is drawn.

steps.detail: Claimed before printing, because a print dialog never says whether a file was saved.
A paid plan, or EXPORT_LIMIT_FREE unset, is uncounted and writes nothing.
Decide and increment in one statement.
The sheet is never put into the page.
Pages are 520×693 CSS px, matching @page, so the PDF comes out 1:1. Any other failure lets the export through.

flows.name: Save & share an issue
flows.summary: Pages are sealed in the browser with a per-issue AES-GCM key and uploaded straight to storage; the key goes in the link after #.

steps.detail: A fresh key per issue, made with WebCrypto.
Page count, how long to keep it, and the key only if 'Keep in My magazines' is on.
1–96 pages; an editable copy must keep its key on the account.
Forever is for paid plans only.
Owner, page count, expiry, optional key. No title, no words.

steps.text: 201 · id + one upload slot per file
seal() each page and the manifest
steps.detail: 1080×1440 carousel slides; title and dek live inside the sealed manifest.

steps.text: PUT sealed blobs to signed URLs
steps.detail: Bytes never pass through the API.
Checked against the bucket, not taken on trust.
The row stays unready; the hourly sweep clears it after a day.
The key sits after the #, which browsers never send to a server.

flows.name: Open a shared link
flows.summary: Anyone with the link can read it, with no account; the server hands out sealed bytes it cannot open.

steps.detail: Only the id travels; no sign-in on this route.
Expiry is checked on every read, so an issue is unreachable the moment it expires.
Says nothing about whether it ever existed.
AES-GCM decrypt in the browser.

steps.text: This link's key does not open the magazine
GET each sealed page as it's turned to
steps.detail: Pages are opened on demand, not all 96 up front.

flows.name: Subscribe with Dodo
flows.summary: Checkout only hands out a URL; the webhook is the only thing that grants a plan.

steps.detail: Paid-plan buttons are on only with BUN_PUBLIC_CHECKOUT=on.
A second checkout would bill twice; the portal is where plan changes happen.
The reader is sent to manage the plan they hold.
metadata.supabase_user_id lets the webhook map the payment back.
Raw body parser mounted before express.json so the signature sees the original bytes.
Needs webhook-id, -signature and -timestamp.
From metadata, else by dodo_customer_id; links the customer id.
Idempotent on the Dodo subscription id; unknown products are skipped.
Append-only ledger with no foreign key to subscriptions: webhooks arrive out of order.

flows.name: Speak a story (live)
flows.summary: The API only mints a one-use key; audio streams from the browser straight to OpenAI.

steps.detail: Open to everyone for now (VOICE_NEEDS_SIGN_IN = false).
Counted per IP when signed out, in memory.
Resets at midnight UTC.
Expires 60 seconds after it's made; server VAD and near-field noise reduction.
24 kHz PCM from the microphone; never touches the Atlas server.
Written live into the Write box.

flows.name: Submit and review a layout
flows.summary: The one place a design is kept: rebuilt server-side with every photo dropped and every word replaced, plus one consented sample picture.

steps.detail: Kind, title, description, the design and one sample picture; its own larger JSON parser.
Photos dropped, words replaced with placeholders, colours, fonts and numbers validated; 200 KB cap.
If the insert fails the sample is removed again.
Accept or reject, with an optional note.
Only when RESEND_API_KEY and EMAIL_FROM are set; 15 s timeout; a failure just leaves notified_at empty.

flows.name: Hourly clean-up and keep-alive
flows.summary: setInterval jobs inside the API process, started once it is listening.

steps.detail: Keeps the Render service from idling; uses RENDER_EXTERNAL_URL or KEEPALIVE_URL. 30s timeout.

steps.text: SELECT issues expired or unready > 1 day
steps.detail: Hourly, and once at boot so a restart catches up. 100 at a time.
Files first, rows second, so a failure leaves a row the next sweep retries.
issue_members go with them.
Edits begun and never committed.
Every 6 hours.
The row and the decision stay; only the picture goes.

components.name: Desk and magazine engine
components.role: Composes the issue by measuring real type (fit.ts) and pours it through layouts; photos stay object URLs.

components.name: Static site
components.role: Serves prerendered pages and rewrites /api/* to api.ouratlas.co.in.

components.name: API
components.role: Auth checks, allowances, AI calls, saved-issue bookkeeping, billing and webhooks. Every integration is optional and returns 503 when unconfigured.

components.name: Cron
components.role: Keep-alive ping, saved-issue prune, rejected-sample prune.

components.name: Supabase
components.tech: Auth, Postgres with RLS, private storage
components.role: Accounts (Google sign-in), subscriptions, counters, saved-issue rows, two private buckets. The API uses the service-role key after resolving the user.

components.name: AI providers
components.role: Editor (Opus 5.5 by default), copy desk (OpenAI by default), transcription (OpenAI gpt-4o-transcribe).

components.name: Billing
components.role: Checkout and portal; webhooks are the only writers of subscriptions and payments.

components.name: Android app
components.role: Loads the same bundle and calls the API cross-origin, which api/cors.ts allows.

unknowns: Render region and instance count aren't in the repository; the in-memory burst and daily limits are per process, so they loosen with more than one instance (api/limits.ts says so).
Supabase project region and plan aren't in the repository.
No error tracking or metrics service: failures are console.error lines in the host's log.
The open voice routes count by IP from X-Forwarded-For with trust proxy on, which is spoofable when the API host is called directly (api/limits.ts notes this).
No automated tests run in CI beyond typecheck, build and a boot check; two small test files exist under api/.
The Stripe flow mirrors the Dodo one but isn't drawn here; Dodo is the live provider.
